key_insight: Equilibrated flux estimators can give a guaranteed, fully computable upper bound on finite-element energy error even for coarse or badly distorted meshes, without relying on shape-regularity assumptions.
engineering_relevance: This makes it possible to quantify simulation reliability on real-world geometries and poor-quality meshes, where classical a posteriori error estimates may not apply.
method: Build an equilibrated flux estimator for the energy-norm discretization error
Use only a local Poincaré constant on each cell; no shape-regularity, quasi-uniformity, or angle condition is needed
Apply the Payne–Weinberger bound on convex cells to keep the estimator computable
evidence_signal: The abstract argues analytically that reliability is guaranteed with constant one, while mesh distortion mainly affects local efficiency rather than correctness.
watch_item: The estimator can become pessimistic on highly distorted meshes, so it may overestimate error even though it remains reliable.
paper_title: A posteriori error estimation for coarse or distorted meshes
